verdict.headline: Rey Cortiço Lunch
verdict.reason: Rey Cortiço is worth a quick check for lunch, but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide should let the sandbars work without overdoing it.

conversationalSummary.text: For TODAY, I’d keep it check-first at Rey Cortiço around lunch. The cams matter here, because Surfline looks only poor-to-fair and the wind angle isn’t really lined up for the spot, so it can get choppy fast. I’m thinking dead low might still give you a chance if the sandbanks line up, but I’d only leave if Surfline or MEO Beachcam shows it looking noticeably cleaner than expected.

best.explanation: Rey Cortiço looks like a small north coast window for Rare window, Medium confidence: 0.3-0.6 m, 19 kJ, 9 s period, lully 0/100, and wind is the main risk.  An open beach break where the sandbanks decide everything; this is best for quiet, punchy peaks when Lagide is too small; 6-9s at low tide can still work on Belgas if the sandbars are lined up, so checking exposed beaches makes sense.  Watch: Surfline consistency is lully; wind angle is poor for this spot.
